summary: Umrah has four parts, always performed in this order: enter **ihram** with the intention before you cross the miqat; perform **tawaf**, seven anticlockwise circuits of the Kaaba starting at the Black Stone; walk **sa'i**, seven laps between Safa and Marwah; then **shave or trim your hair**. The rites themselves take a few hours, depending on the crowds.

items.label: Rites
items.value: Ihram, tawaf, sa'i, halq or taqsir

items.label: When
items.value: Through the year, except a pause around Hajj

blocks.text: Umrah is often called the "lesser pilgrimage". Unlike Hajj, it is not tied to particular dates, and its rites are completed in one visit to Masjid al-Haram. The four schools of Islamic law classify the parts slightly differently (some as pillars, some as obligations), but all of them perform the same acts in the same order. This guide follows that shared sequence. Where scholars differ on a detail, we say so, and your group's guide or a scholar you trust can advise you.
The four rites in order

items.title: Ihram and intention
items.text: Put on ihram clothing, make the intention for Umrah before the miqat and begin reciting the talbiyah.

items.title: Tawaf
items.text: Walk seven circuits around the Kaaba, anticlockwise, starting and ending at the Black Stone corner. Then pray two rak'ahs.

items.title: Sa'i
items.text: Walk seven laps between the hills of Safa and Marwah, starting at Safa and finishing at Marwah.

items.title: Halq or taqsir
items.text: Men shave the head or trim the hair; women cut a fingertip's length. Your Umrah is complete and the restrictions of ihram end.

blocks.text: Step 1: Ihram and the miqat

**Ihram** is the sacred state a pilgrim enters for Umrah or Hajj, and also the name for the simple clothing worn in it. You must be in ihram before you cross a **miqat**, one of the boundary points around Makkah set for pilgrims.
Preparing for ihram

items: Take a bath (ghusl), clip your nails and remove unwanted body hair. These are recommended (sunnah), not conditions.
**Men** wear two plain, unstitched white sheets: one wrapped around the waist (izar) and one over the shoulders (rida). Footwear should leave the top of the foot uncovered.
**Women** wear their normal modest clothing in any colour. The face and hands stay uncovered in ihram, so no niqab and no gloves.
Men may apply perfume to the body, not the clothes, before making the intention. Once in ihram, no perfume of any kind.
Many pilgrims pray two rak'ahs before making the intention, if it is not a time when voluntary prayer is disliked.

blocks.text: Making the intention when flying from India

Flights from India to Jeddah cross a miqat in the air before landing, so you must be in ihram on the plane. In practice, men change into ihram at home or at the departure airport, and pilgrims make the intention on board when the crew announces that the miqat is near. Do not wait until you land in Jeddah: Jeddah is inside the miqat boundary. If your group flies to **Madinah first**, you do not need ihram on the flight. You will put it on in Madinah before travelling to Makkah, and make the intention at the Madinah miqat (Dhul Hulayfah, also called Abyar Ali).
To make the intention, say: **"Labbayka Allahumma 'umratan"** ("Here I am, O Allah, for Umrah"). Then begin the talbiyah, repeating it often (men aloud, women quietly) until you start tawaf.

blocks.arabic: لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ
blocks.transliteration: Labbayk Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk. Innal-hamda wan-ni'mata laka wal-mulk, la sharika lak.
blocks.translation: Here I am, O Allah, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. All praise, all blessings and all sovereignty belong to You. You have no partner.
blocks.cite: The talbiyah, as reported in Sahih al-Bukhari 1549

blocks.text: What is not allowed in ihram

items: **Everyone:** perfume or scented products (including scented soap, wipes and creams), cutting hair or nails, marital relations, a marriage contract, hunting, and quarrelling or bad language.
**Men:** stitched or fitted clothing (shirts, trousers, underwear, socks) and covering the head.
**Women:** covering the face with a niqab and wearing gloves.

blocks.text: If you break a rule of ihram by mistake, or are unsure whether you did, ask your group's guide or a scholar. Some mistakes need a compensation (fidyah), and the ruling depends on what happened and on your school of thought.

image.alt: Five men in white ihram standing together outside a hotel entrance with the Makkah skyline behind
image.caption: Men in the two white sheets of ihram, Makkah.

blocks.text: Step 2: Tawaf around the Kaaba
Enter Masjid al-Haram with your right foot and the dua for entering a mosque. You need **wudu** for tawaf. Stop reciting the talbiyah when you begin.

items: **Men uncover the right shoulder** by passing the upper sheet under the right arm (idtiba). This is only for the tawaf of Umrah; cover the shoulder again afterwards.

**Start at the Black Stone** (al-Hajar al-Aswad). A green light on the wall of the mosque marks its line. Face the Black Stone, raise your right hand towards it and say "Bismillah, Allahu akbar". You do not need to touch or kiss it, and you should not push through the crowd to do so.
**Walk anticlockwise**, keeping the Kaaba on your left. Each time you return to the Black Stone line, one circuit is complete. Do seven.
**Stay outside the semicircular wall** (Hijr Ismail) next to the Kaaba: the area inside it is part of the Kaaba, so a circuit through it does not count.
Men walk briskly with short steps (raml) in the **first three circuits**, if the crowd allows.
There is no fixed dua for each circuit. Pray in any language. Between the Yemeni corner and the Black Stone, it is sunnah to recite the verse below.

blocks.arabic: رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
blocks.transliteration: Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhaban-nar.
blocks.translation: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.

blocks.text: After the seventh circuit, cover your right shoulder and **pray two rak'ahs**, behind Maqam Ibrahim if there is space, or anywhere else in the mosque. Then drink **Zamzam** water. Coolers stand throughout the mosque.

blocks.title: If you lose count
blocks.text: Go with the lower number you are sure of. If you completed four circuits for certain and might have done five, count four and continue. The ground floor around the Kaaba (the mataf) is busiest; the upper floors are calmer, but each circuit there is much longer.

image.alt: Meezan pilgrims in white ihram and abayas posing in front of the Kaaba in Makkah
image.caption: A Meezan group in front of the Kaaba after tawaf.

blocks.text: Step 3: Sa'i between Safa and Marwah

Sa'i remembers Hajar, the mother of Ismail, who ran between these two hills searching for water. Today both hills sit inside the mosque, joined by a long air-conditioned gallery with separate levels and lanes for wheelchairs. Follow the signs to Safa.

items: As you approach Safa, it is sunnah to recite: "Innas-Safa wal-Marwata min sha'a'irillah" (Indeed, Safa and Marwah are among the symbols of Allah, Quran 2:158).
On Safa, face the Kaaba, raise your hands, praise Allah and make dua.
Walk to Marwah. That is **one lap**. Walking back to Safa is the second. You finish at **Marwah after the seventh lap**.
Between the two **green lights** on the route, men jog lightly. Women walk at a normal pace throughout.
On Marwah, face the Kaaba and make dua again, as on Safa.

blocks.text: Seven laps add up to a little over three kilometres. Wudu is recommended for sa'i but, according to most scholars, not required. There is no special prayer after sa'i.
Step 4: Halq or taqsir

Leaving sa'i at Marwah, you will find barbers nearby. **Men** either shave the whole head (halq, which carries greater reward) or trim the hair evenly from across the head (taqsir). **Women** gather their hair and cut about a fingertip's length from the ends; a family member or a woman in your group can help in your room. Do not cut your hair before sa'i is finished.
With this, your **Umrah is complete**. The restrictions of ihram are lifted and you may change into normal clothes.

blocks.title: Go through each step with a guide
blocks.text: Meezan pilgrims attend a briefing before departure, and our group leaders accompany them through the rites in Makkah.
Common mistakes first-timers make

items: **Crossing the miqat without ihram**, for example by planning to change in Jeddah. Be in ihram before the plane reaches the miqat.
**Starting tawaf away from the Black Stone line.** A circuit begins and ends there; use the green light as your marker.
**Walking through Hijr Ismail** during tawaf, which makes that circuit incomplete.
**Keeping the right shoulder bare** after tawaf, including in prayer. It is uncovered only during the tawaf itself.
**Using scented products** in ihram: perfumed soap, shampoo, wet wipes or deodorant. Pack unscented versions.
**Pushing to touch the Black Stone.** Raising your hand towards it from a distance is enough.
**Cutting only a few strands** of hair. Men should shave or trim evenly from across the head.

blocks.text: Practical tips for the day

items: Masjid al-Haram's gates are **numbered and named**. Note the gate you entered by and agree a meeting point with your group.
Carry your shoes in a small cloth bag rather than leaving them at the door. You may not leave by the same gate.
Wear **sandals you have already walked in**. Expect several kilometres on foot.
Drink water regularly, especially in the warmer months, and rest between tawaf and sa'i if you need to.
Elderly pilgrims or those with limited mobility can perform tawaf and sa'i in a **wheelchair**. Tell your group leader in advance; read our [guide to Umrah with family](/blog/umrah-with-family).
Keep your phone charged and your group leader's number saved.

blocks.text: Many pilgrims also spend part of the trip in Madinah to pray at Masjid an-Nabawi. That visit is not part of Umrah, but most packages include it. Our guide to [what to know before travelling to Makkah and Madinah](/blog/first-umrah-things-to-know) covers both cities.

faqs.q: How long does it take to perform Umrah?
faqs.a: The rites themselves (tawaf, sa'i and cutting the hair) usually take a few hours, depending on crowds and on how fast you walk. Most Umrah trips from India last around two weeks so that pilgrims can spend time in both Makkah and Madinah.

faqs.q: What should I recite during tawaf?
faqs.a: There is no fixed dua for each circuit. You may recite the Quran, praise Allah or make dua in any language. Between the Yemeni corner and the Black Stone, it is sunnah to recite "Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah..." (Quran 2:201).

faqs.q: Can a woman perform Umrah during her period?
faqs.a: She can enter ihram and make the intention, but she should not perform tawaf until her period has ended and she has bathed. The other parts follow tawaf. If your travel dates are fixed, discuss your situation with a scholar before you travel.

faqs.q: Is visiting Madinah part of Umrah?
faqs.a: No. Umrah is completed in Makkah. Visiting Masjid an-Nabawi in Madinah is a separate, highly valued visit, and most Umrah packages from India include several days there.

faqs.q: Can I perform Umrah at any time of year?
faqs.a: Umrah can be performed through the year, but Saudi Arabia pauses Umrah for international visitors around the Hajj season. See our guide to the [best time to perform Umrah](/blog/best-time-for-umrah).
